Creators
● Influencer marketing agency

Influencer marketing that picks fit over followers.

Creators shortlisted for audience fit, briefed against one idea, contracted with clear usage rights, and read against sales.

See the work

In short

Influencer marketing is the work of partnering with creators whose audience matches your buyers, so their content introduces and recommends your product.

Monday Marketing Company (MMC) plans influencer and creator partnerships for D2C brands, and can reuse the best content as paid ads.

  • Fit over reachCreators chosen for who follows them, not how many.
  • Tracked properlyLinks and codes so results can be read against sales.
  • Rights agreedTerms that allow the best content to run as ads.
Where influencer marketing goes wrong

Five ways influencer marketing goes wrong.

Creators can introduce a brand well or waste a budget. Each stage below is where it goes wrong, and how we run it.

  1. 1
    Stage 1 of 5Choose for fit

    Picking creators by follower count.

    A large audience that does not match your buyer produces reach, not sales.

    What we do

    We shortlist creators by audience fit, engagement quality and past content, and check them before you commit.

    Creator shortlisting
  2. 2
    Stage 2 of 5Brief around one idea

    Sending a product and hoping for the best.

    Creators know their audience, but need to know the one thing you want said, and what to avoid.

    What we do

    We write clear briefs around a single brand idea, leaving room for the creator's own voice.

    Creative briefs
  3. 3
    Stage 3 of 5Agree the terms

    Paying for a post with no rights to reuse it.

    If you cannot run the content as an ad, you lose its best use.

    What we do

    We agree deliverables, timelines and usage rights up front, including the right to run the content as ads.

    Contracts and usage rights
  4. 4
    Stage 4 of 5Track it to sales

    Judging campaigns on views and likes.

    Views do not show whether anyone bought. Links, codes and blended sales do.

    What we do

    We give each creator tracked links and codes and read results alongside your total sales.

    Tracking and attribution
  5. 5
    Stage 5 of 5Reuse the best

    Letting a great post disappear after a day.

    A post that earned attention organically often works as an ad too.

    What we do

    We take the best creator content, with agreed rights, and run it as paid ads.

    Content reuse as ads

How it works

How we run creator work, step by step.

  1. 1Days 1 to 30

    Shortlist for fit

    Creators chosen by audience fit and content quality, not follower count.

    You getA shortlist you can approve.

  2. 2Days 31 to 60

    Brief and contract

    One idea, clear deliverables and usage rights agreed up front.

    You getContent and terms in writing.

  3. 3Days 61 to 90

    Results are read against sales, and the best content is reused as ads.

    You getSpend that is read against orders.

The days show the order of the work, not a promise of results. What we find in your account decides how long each part takes.

Who it is for

Creators for brands that can measure the result.

Good fit

You sell a product a creator can show, and you can track sales.

D2C brands get creator content that doubles as ad creative, and consumer-facing education and B2B brands can use it for trust.

Not a fit

You want reach with no tracking, or one big name to fix everything.

Fit and tracking decide results, and a big name rarely substitutes for either.

Common questions

Questions about influencer marketing.

What is influencer marketing?

Influencer marketing is the work of partnering with creators whose audience matches your buyers, so their content introduces and recommends your product.

How does influencer marketing work with MMC?

We shortlist for audience fit, brief against one idea, help agree deliverables and usage rights, track results to sales and reuse the best content as ads. Creators disclose paid partnerships as advertising rules require.

What does influencer marketing cost?

A monthly scope, agreed after a call. It is written down so you can see what each month covers. We do not publish a price list, because the right scope depends on your site, your market and how much you want done.

Do you guarantee results?

No. We cannot guarantee reach or sales from any creator. We commit to choosing for fit, clear terms, tracking and honest reporting.

Who is influencer marketing for?

D2C brands that sell products a creator can show. It also applies to B2B and education brands: the same method, measured on qualified leads, enquiries and admissions instead of orders.

What do you need from us?

Your product, brand guidelines, a budget range for creators, tracking set up on your store, and a person who can approve briefs.
